name: Horowitz-Ross Naked Black Holes
description: Large static black holes, charged and close to extremality, in theories with a dilaton, whose curvature invariants are small near the horizon and whose tidal forces crush a falling body outside it. Gary T. Horowitz and Simon F. Ross found them in 1997 among the dilaton black holes of any coupling, the black holes with two charges, and the black holes and branes of string theory.
convention: We keep factors of $c$ explicit. The Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.
history: Near the horizon of some large charged black holes the curvature is enormous and almost null, and an observer held at rest measures small components of it, so "all curvature invariants are small near the event horizon" [horowitz1997naked]. An observer falling in from far away passes resting observers ever faster near the horizon, and meets tidal forces outside it that can pass the Planck scale [horowitz1997naked]. Gary T. Horowitz and Simon F. Ross of the University of California, Santa Barbara, found such black holes in 1997 and called them naked black holes, since "the region of large tidal forces is visible to distant observers" [horowitz1997naked]. They are charged, at or close to extremality, and occur in a wide class of theories with scalar fields, among them the supergravity of string theory at low energy [horowitz1997naked, horowitz1998properties]. In the Schwarzschild and Reissner-Nordström black holes the curvature is unchanged by a radial boost, so falling and resting observers measure tidal forces of about the same size [horowitz1997naked]. Horowitz and Ross wrote a static black hole as $ds^2 = -F\,dt^2 + dr^2/F + R^2 d\Omega^2$, and showed that under a radial boost no curvature component is smaller than in the static frame [horowitz1997naked].¶An observer falling in with energy $E$ per unit mass feels across the line of fall the tidal component $R_{0'20'2} = -[R''(E^2 - F) - F'R'/2]/R$, a prime marking a derivative in $r$ [horowitz1997naked]. Near the horizon the static components are of order $1/R^2$, small for a horizon large in Planck units, and a body falling from rest meets tidal forces past the Planck scale where $|R''/R| > 1$ in Planck units [horowitz1997naked]. Horowitz and Ross took as their first example the dilaton black holes of Gary Gibbons and Kei-ichi Maeda, and of David Garfinkle, Horowitz, and Andrew Strominger, in which a scalar field, the dilaton, couples to the Maxwell field with strength $a$ and $R = r(1 - r_-/r)^{a^2/(1+a^2)}$ [gibbons1988, garfinkle1991, horowitz1997naked]. The horizon is at $r_+$, and for $a \neq 0$ a curvature singularity lies at $r_-$, and with $a = 0$ the metric is the Reissner-Nordström metric, with an inner horizon at $r_-$ [horowitz1997naked]. With $\epsilon = 1 - r_-/r_+$, Horowitz and Ross found the hole naked for $\epsilon \ll 1$ and $\epsilon^{-a^2/(1+a^2)} \ll r_+ \ll \epsilon^{-1}$, close to extremality and with a large mass [horowitz1997naked]. At fixed mass the horizon shrinks to zero area in the extremal limit $r_+ = r_-$, with a null singularity for $0 < a \le 1$ and a timelike one for $a > 1$, and they raised the mass as $\epsilon$ fell to keep the horizon large [horowitz1997naked].¶A black hole of mass $M$ with electric charge $Q$ in one Maxwell field and magnetic charge $P$ in another has $R^2 = r^2 - \Sigma^2$, with $\Sigma = (P^2 - Q^2)/2M$, and with both charges present its horizon stays smooth and of finite area at extremality [horowitz1997naked]. Observers falling into it meet large tidal forces outside the horizon when one charge greatly exceeds the other [horowitz1997naked]. In string theory the black hole with winding and momentum charges is naked in its string metric, and so are the black $p$-branes with one Ramond-Ramond charge close to extremality [horowitz1997naked]. At extremality their tidal forces diverge as the radius $r$ falls to zero, except for the three-brane, so branes regular there in the static frame are singular [horowitz1997naked]. Some near extremal black holes whose entropy was counted from string states are naked, and Horowitz and Ross suggested that their tidal forces, which crush a falling body sideways, may invalidate the simple argument for information loss [horowitz1997naked]. Naked black holes leave a strict reading of cosmic censorship intact and "weaken the spirit of cosmic censorship", since quantum gravity could then be visible outside macroscopic black holes [horowitz1997naked].¶Horowitz and Ross found in 1998 that near the horizon of a dilaton black hole the tidal component is close to $a^2/[(1+a^2)^2\tau^2]$, set by the proper time $\tau$ an observer has left before the singularity [horowitz1998properties]. The Weyl tensor of a static spherical black hole is unchanged by radial boosts, and so is its Maxwell stress, so the large components come from the dilaton's stress energy, a nearly null wave that remains just outside the horizon [horowitz1998properties]. A small observer falling in crosses that region as a plane wave of the dilaton, and a string crossing it becomes highly excited and massive yet stays small [horowitz1998properties]. A little infalling matter can raise the curvature invariants to the Planck scale outside the horizon, and they found by an exact calculation for a falling charged shell of dust that neither its path nor the black hole it leaves changes much [horowitz1998properties].¶Ivan Booth and Robert Mann extended the quasilocal energy, the energy within a finite region, in 1999 to fields with a dilaton and to moving observers, and applied it to naked black holes [booth1999static]. Unless the coupling $a$ is very small, observers at rest near the horizon measure small curvature and a large geometric energy, and observers falling in measure large curvature and a small one [booth1999static]. Arthur Lue and Erick J. Weinberg found in 2000 that magnetic monopoles bound by their own gravity, close to forming a horizon outside their core, display what Horowitz and Ross "have termed naked-black-hole behavior, even though there is no black hole at all" [lue2000]. A body falling through the place where that horizon would form feels a tidal force that grows without bound as the monopole nears the threshold [lue2000].¶Oleg Zaslavskii showed in 2007 that a black hole of the kind called "truly naked", whose horizon has a finite Kretschmann scalar and infinite tidal forces in a falling frame, can be spherically symmetric if it is extremal or ultraextremal [zaslavskii2007]. In that scheme the holes of Horowitz and Ross are naked, their tidal forces raised by the boost from zero to finite values, and no nonextremal spherical hole is of that kind [zaslavskii2007]. Hryhorii Ovcharenko and Zaslavskii extended the scheme to rotating black holes in 2025 and found the algebraic types an observer falling into a "truly naked" horizon sees [ovcharenko2025]. Carlos Herdeiro, Eugen Radu, and Etevaldo dos Santos Costa Filho built spinning charged dilaton black holes numerically, and reported in 2026 that for $0 < a < \sqrt{3}$ the fastest spinning reach zero temperature with a finite Kretschmann scalar and infinite tidal forces for a falling observer [herdeiro2026charged]. Jose Luis Blázquez-Salcedo, Herdeiro, Radu, dos Santos Costa Filho, and Kunihito Uzawa found that among the extremal spinning holes of $a = 1$ only those with equal electric and magnetic charges keep their tidal forces finite [blazquez2026spinning].

related.text: The black hole of coupling $a = 1$, the value of string theory, with $r_s = r_+$ and $r_d = r_-$. Close to extremality and with a large horizon it is naked [horowitz1997naked].

The black hole with the dilaton switched off, $a = 0$, where $r_-$ is an inner horizon. Its curvature is unchanged by a radial boost, so an observer falling in meets tidal forces of about the size an observer at rest measures [horowitz1997naked].

The black hole with no charge, $r_- = 0$. Its curvature is unchanged by a radial boost, so an observer falling in from rest feels the tidal forces an observer at rest measures there [horowitz1997naked].

The black hole of coupling $a = \sqrt{3}$, the coupling of Kaluza and Klein's theory reduced to four dimensions, is the four dimensional metric of their charged hole, with $r$ shifted by $r_-$ [herdeiro2026charged]. Set spinning, it keeps its tidal forces finite at zero temperature [herdeiro2026charged].

The black hole of five dimensions with three charges, whose entropy and radiation strings and D-branes explain, is naked when one charge is much smaller than another and the horizon is large [horowitz1997naked].

The black branes with one Ramond-Ramond charge are naked close to extremality. At extremality the three-brane alone among them keeps its tidal forces finite as its radius falls to zero, as its smooth extension through the horizon requires [horowitz1997naked].

coordinates.name: Dilaton Coupling $a$

parameters.description: Radius of the event horizon, a length
Radius of the singularity, a length, with $r_+r_- = (1 + a^2)Q^2$ for the charge $Q$ in units with $G = c = 1$; $r_- = r_+$ is the extremal limit, and $r_- = 0$ is Schwarzschild's black hole

Coupling of the dilaton to the Maxwell field, a pure number; $a = 1$ is the coupling of string theory, $a = \sqrt{3}$ that of Kaluza and Klein's theory, and $a = 0$ is Reissner and Nordström's black hole, whose $r_-$ is an inner horizon
Areal radius, a length: the sphere through each point has area $4\pi R^2$

coordinates.convention: We use the coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$ of Horowitz and Ross [horowitz1997naked], with $t$ having dimensions of time, and take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$. A dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter $\lambda$, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.
coordinates.line_element: ds^2 = -\dfrac{\left(r - r_+\right)\left(r - r_-\right)}{R^2}c^2dt^2 + \dfrac{R^2\,dr^2}{\left(r - r_+\right)\left(r - r_-\right)} + R^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)

nonzero.value: \dfrac{r\,r_+ + r\,r_- - 2r_+\,r_- + r\,r_+\,a^2 - r\,r_-\,a^2}{2r\left(1 + a^2\right)\left(r - r_+\right)\left(r - r_-\right)}
\dfrac{r\,r_+ + r\,r_- - 2r_+\,r_- + r\,r_+\,a^2 - r\,r_-\,a^2}{2r\left(1 + a^2\right)\left(r - r_+\right)\left(r - r_-\right)}
-\dfrac{r\,r_+ + r\,r_- - 2r_+\,r_- + r\,r_+\,a^2 - r\,r_-\,a^2}{2r\left(1 + a^2\right)\left(r - r_+\right)\left(r - r_-\right)}
\dfrac{\left(r - r_+\right)\left(r - r_-\right)\left(r\,r_+ + r\,r_- - 2r_+\,r_- + r\,r_+\,a^2 - r\,r_-\,a^2\right)}{2r\,R^4\left(1 + a^2\right)}
-\dfrac{R^2\left(r\,r_+ + r\,r_- - 2r_+\,r_- + r\,r_+\,a^2 - r\,r_-\,a^2\right)}{2r\left(1 + a^2\right)\left(r - r_+\right)^2\left(r - r_-\right)^2}
-\dfrac{\left(r - r_- + r\,a^2\right)\left(r\,r_+ + r\,r_- - 2r_+\,r_- + r\,r_+\,a^2 - r\,r_-\,a^2\right)}{2r^2\left(1 + a^2\right)^2\left(r - r_-\right)}
\dfrac{\left(r - r_- + r\,a^2\right)\left(r\,r_+ + r\,r_- - 2r_+\,r_- + r\,r_+\,a^2 - r\,r_-\,a^2\right)}{2r^2\left(1 + a^2\right)^2\left(r - r_-\right)}
-\dfrac{\left(r - r_- + r\,a^2\right)\left(r\,r_+ + r\,r_- - 2r_+\,r_- + r\,r_+\,a^2 - r\,r_-\,a^2\right)\sin^2\theta}{2r^2\left(1 + a^2\right)^2\left(r - r_-\right)}
\dfrac{\left(r - r_- + r\,a^2\right)\left(r\,r_+ + r\,r_- - 2r_+\,r_- + r\,r_+\,a^2 - r\,r_-\,a^2\right)\sin^2\theta}{2r^2\left(1 + a^2\right)^2\left(r - r_-\right)}
-\dfrac{\left(r - r_+\right)\left(r - r_- + r\,a^2\right)\left(r\,r_+ + r\,r_- - 2r_+\,r_- + r\,r_+\,a^2 - r\,r_-\,a^2\right)}{2r^2\,R^4\left(1 + a^2\right)^2}
\dfrac{\left(r - r_+\right)\left(r - r_- + r\,a^2\right)\left(r\,r_+ + r\,r_- - 2r_+\,r_- + r\,r_+\,a^2 - r\,r_-\,a^2\right)}{2r^2\,R^4\left(1 + a^2\right)^2}
-\dfrac{\left(r - r_+\right)\left(r - r_- + r\,a^2\right)\left(r\,r_+ + r\,r_- - 2r_+\,r_- + r\,r_+\,a^2 - r\,r_-\,a^2\right)}{2r^2\,R^4\left(1 + a^2\right)^2}
\dfrac{\left(r - r_+\right)\left(r - r_- + r\,a^2\right)\left(r\,r_+ + r\,r_- - 2r_+\,r_- + r\,r_+\,a^2 - r\,r_-\,a^2\right)}{2r^2\,R^4\left(1 + a^2\right)^2}
\dfrac{\left(r - r_+\right)\left(r - r_- + r\,a^2\right)\left(r\,r_+ + r\,r_- - 2r_+\,r_- + r\,r_+\,a^2 - r\,r_-\,a^2\right)}{2r^2\,R^2\left(1 + a^2\right)^2}
-\dfrac{\left(r - r_+\right)\left(r - r_- + r\,a^2\right)\left(r\,r_+ + r\,r_- - 2r_+\,r_- + r\,r_+\,a^2 - r\,r_-\,a^2\right)}{2r^2\,R^2\left(1 + a^2\right)^2}
-\dfrac{\left(r - r_+\right)\left(r - r_- + r\,a^2\right)\left(r\,r_+ + r\,r_- - 2r_+\,r_- + r\,r_+\,a^2 - r\,r_-\,a^2\right)}{2r^2\,R^2\left(1 + a^2\right)^2}
\dfrac{\left(r - r_+\right)\left(r - r_- + r\,a^2\right)\left(r\,r_+ + r\,r_- - 2r_+\,r_- + r\,r_+\,a^2 - r\,r_-\,a^2\right)}{2r^2\,R^2\left(1 + a^2\right)^2}
\dfrac{\left(r - r_+\right)\left(r - r_- + r\,a^2\right)\left(r\,r_+ + r\,r_- - 2r_+\,r_- + r\,r_+\,a^2 - r\,r_-\,a^2\right)\sin^2\theta}{2r^2\,R^2\left(1 + a^2\right)^2}
-\dfrac{\left(r - r_+\right)\left(r - r_- + r\,a^2\right)\left(r\,r_+ + r\,r_- - 2r_+\,r_- + r\,r_+\,a^2 - r\,r_-\,a^2\right)\sin^2\theta}{2r^2\,R^2\left(1 + a^2\right)^2}
-\dfrac{\left(r - r_+\right)\left(r - r_- + r\,a^2\right)\left(r\,r_+ + r\,r_- - 2r_+\,r_- + r\,r_+\,a^2 - r\,r_-\,a^2\right)\sin^2\theta}{2r^2\,R^2\left(1 + a^2\right)^2}
\dfrac{\left(r - r_+\right)\left(r - r_- + r\,a^2\right)\left(r\,r_+ + r\,r_- - 2r_+\,r_- + r\,r_+\,a^2 - r\,r_-\,a^2\right)\sin^2\theta}{2r^2\,R^2\left(1 + a^2\right)^2}
-\dfrac{R^2\left(r^2\,r_+ + r^2\,r_- - 3r\,r_+\,r_- - r\,r_-^2 + 2r_+\,r_-^2 + r^2\,r_+\,a^2 - r^2\,r_-\,a^2\right)\sin^2\theta}{2r^2\left(1 + a^2\right)\left(r - r_+\right)\left(r - r_-\right)^2}
\dfrac{R^2\left(r^2\,r_+ + r^2\,r_- - 3r\,r_+\,r_- - r\,r_-^2 + 2r_+\,r_-^2 + r^2\,r_+\,a^2 - r^2\,r_-\,a^2\right)\sin^2\theta}{2r^2\left(1 + a^2\right)\left(r - r_+\right)\left(r - r_-\right)^2}
\dfrac{R^2\left(r^2\,r_+ + r^2\,r_- - 3r\,r_+\,r_- - r\,r_-^2 + 2r_+\,r_-^2 + r^2\,r_+\,a^2 - r^2\,r_-\,a^2\right)\sin^2\theta}{2r^2\left(1 + a^2\right)\left(r - r_+\right)\left(r - r_-\right)^2}
-\dfrac{R^2\left(r^2\,r_+ + r^2\,r_- - 3r\,r_+\,r_- - r\,r_-^2 + 2r_+\,r_-^2 + r^2\,r_+\,a^2 - r^2\,r_-\,a^2\right)\sin^2\theta}{2r^2\left(1 + a^2\right)\left(r - r_+\right)\left(r - r_-\right)^2}
-\dfrac{r_-\left(r\,r_+ - r_+\,r_- + r\,r_+\,a^2 - 2r\,r_-\,a^2 + r_+\,r_-\,a^2\right)}{r^2\left(1 + a^2\right)^2\left(r - r_+\right)\left(r - r_-\right)^2}
-\dfrac{r_-\left(r\,r_+ - r_+\,r_- + r\,r_+\,a^2 - r\,r_-\,a^2\right)}{r^2\left(1 + a^2\right)^2\left(r - r_+\right)\left(r - r_-\right)^2}
\dfrac{r_-\left(r\,r_+ - r_+\,r_- + r\,r_+\,a^2 + r\,r_-\,a^2 - 2r_+\,r_-\,a^2\right)}{r^2\left(1 + a^2\right)^2\left(r - r_+\right)\left(r - r_-\right)^2}

geodesics: \ddot{t} + \dfrac{r\,r_+ + r\,r_- - 2r_+\,r_- + r\,r_+\,a^2 - r\,r_-\,a^2}{r\left(1 + a^2\right)\left(r - r_+\right)\left(r - r_-\right)}\dot{t}\dot{r} = 0

\ddot{r} + \dfrac{\left(r - r_+\right)\left(r - r_-\right)\left(r\,r_+ + r\,r_- - 2r_+\,r_- + r\,r_+\,a^2 - r\,r_-\,a^2\right)}{2r\,R^4\left(1 + a^2\right)}\dot{t}^2 - \dfrac{r\,r_+ + r\,r_- - 2r_+\,r_- + r\,r_+\,a^2 - r\,r_-\,a^2}{2r\left(1 + a^2\right)\left(r - r_+\right)\left(r - r_-\right)}\dot{r}^2 - \dfrac{\left(r - r_+\right)\left(r - r_- + r\,a^2\right)}{r\left(1 + a^2\right)}\dot{\theta}^2 - \dfrac{\left(r - r_+\right)\left(r - r_- + r\,a^2\right)\sin^2\theta}{r\left(1 + a^2\right)}\dot{\phi}^2 = 0

coordinates.name: Electric and Magnetic Charges

parameters.description: Radius of the event horizon, a length
Radius of the inner horizon, a length; $r_- = r_+$ is the extremal limit

Length set by the mass $M$, the electric charge $Q$, and the magnetic charge $P$, $\Sigma = (P^2 - Q^2)/2M$, with $r_\pm = M \pm (M^2 + \Sigma^2 - Q^2 - P^2)^{1/2}$ in units with $G = c = 1$; $\Sigma = 0$ is Reissner and Nordström's black hole, and $|\Sigma| = r_-$ the black hole of one charge

coordinates.convention: We use the coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$ of Horowitz and Ross's black hole with two Maxwell fields [horowitz1997naked], with $t$ having dimensions of time, and take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$. A dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter $\lambda$, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.
geodesics: \ddot{r} + \dfrac{\left(r - r_+\right)\left(r - r_-\right)\left(r^2\,r_+ + r^2\,r_- - 2r\,r_+\,r_- - 2r\,\Sigma^2 + r_+\,\Sigma^2 + r_-\,\Sigma^2\right)}{2\left(r + \Sigma\right)^3\left(r - \Sigma\right)^3}\dot{t}^2 - \dfrac{r^2\,r_+ + r^2\,r_- - 2r\,r_+\,r_- - 2r\,\Sigma^2 + r_+\,\Sigma^2 + r_-\,\Sigma^2}{2\left(r + \Sigma\right)\left(r - \Sigma\right)\left(r - r_+\right)\left(r - r_-\right)}\dot{r}^2 - \dfrac{r\left(r - r_+\right)\left(r - r_-\right)}{\left(r + \Sigma\right)\left(r - \Sigma\right)}\dot{\theta}^2 - \dfrac{r\left(r - r_+\right)\left(r - r_-\right)\sin^2\theta}{\left(r + \Sigma\right)\left(r - \Sigma\right)}\dot{\phi}^2 = 0

coordinates.name: String Metric, Winding and Momentum

parameters.description: Radius of the event horizon, a length
Winding length, $r_1 = r_0\sinh^2\gamma_1$ for the parameter $\gamma_1$ of the winding charge of the string, proportional to $\sinh 2\gamma_1$
Momentum length, $r_p = r_0\sinh^2\gamma_p$ for the parameter $\gamma_p$ of the momentum charge along the circle the string winds, proportional to $\sinh 2\gamma_p$

coordinates.convention: We use the coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$ of Horowitz and Ross on the string metric $g_{\mu\nu}$ of the black hole [horowitz1997naked], with $t$ having dimensions of time, and take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$. The Einstein metric is $e^{-2\varphi}g_{\mu\nu}$, with the dilaton $e^{-2\varphi} = \sqrt{(r + r_1)(r + r_p)}/r$. A dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter $\lambda$, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.
coordinates.line_element: ds^2 = -\dfrac{r\left(r - r_0\right)}{\left(r + r_1\right)\left(r + r_p\right)}c^2dt^2 + \dfrac{r\,dr^2}{r - r_0} + r^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)

nonzero.value: \dfrac{r^2\,r_0 + r^2\,r_1 + r^2\,r_p + 2r\,r_1\,r_p - r_0\,r_1\,r_p}{2r\left(r + r_1\right)\left(r + r_p\right)\left(r - r_0\right)}
\dfrac{r^2\,r_0 + r^2\,r_1 + r^2\,r_p + 2r\,r_1\,r_p - r_0\,r_1\,r_p}{2r\left(r + r_1\right)\left(r + r_p\right)\left(r - r_0\right)}
\dfrac{\left(r - r_0\right)\left(r^2\,r_0 + r^2\,r_1 + r^2\,r_p + 2r\,r_1\,r_p - r_0\,r_1\,r_p\right)}{2r\left(r + r_1\right)^2\left(r + r_p\right)^2}
-\dfrac{\left(r - r_0\right)\left(r^2\,r_0 + r^2\,r_1 + r^2\,r_p + 2r\,r_1\,r_p - r_0\,r_1\,r_p\right)}{2r^2\left(r + r_1\right)^2\left(r + r_p\right)^2}
\dfrac{\left(r - r_0\right)\left(r^2\,r_0 + r^2\,r_1 + r^2\,r_p + 2r\,r_1\,r_p - r_0\,r_1\,r_p\right)}{2r^2\left(r + r_1\right)^2\left(r + r_p\right)^2}
-\dfrac{\left(r - r_0\right)\left(r^2\,r_0 + r^2\,r_1 + r^2\,r_p + 2r\,r_1\,r_p - r_0\,r_1\,r_p\right)}{2r^2\left(r + r_1\right)^2\left(r + r_p\right)^2}
\dfrac{\left(r - r_0\right)\left(r^2\,r_0 + r^2\,r_1 + r^2\,r_p + 2r\,r_1\,r_p - r_0\,r_1\,r_p\right)}{2r^2\left(r + r_1\right)^2\left(r + r_p\right)^2}
\dfrac{\left(r - r_0\right)\left(r^2\,r_0 + r^2\,r_1 + r^2\,r_p + 2r\,r_1\,r_p - r_0\,r_1\,r_p\right)}{2\left(r + r_1\right)^2\left(r + r_p\right)^2}
-\dfrac{\left(r - r_0\right)\left(r^2\,r_0 + r^2\,r_1 + r^2\,r_p + 2r\,r_1\,r_p - r_0\,r_1\,r_p\right)}{2\left(r + r_1\right)^2\left(r + r_p\right)^2}
-\dfrac{\left(r - r_0\right)\left(r^2\,r_0 + r^2\,r_1 + r^2\,r_p + 2r\,r_1\,r_p - r_0\,r_1\,r_p\right)}{2\left(r + r_1\right)^2\left(r + r_p\right)^2}
\dfrac{\left(r - r_0\right)\left(r^2\,r_0 + r^2\,r_1 + r^2\,r_p + 2r\,r_1\,r_p - r_0\,r_1\,r_p\right)}{2\left(r + r_1\right)^2\left(r + r_p\right)^2}

geodesics: \ddot{t} + \dfrac{r^2\,r_0 + r^2\,r_1 + r^2\,r_p + 2r\,r_1\,r_p - r_0\,r_1\,r_p}{r\left(r + r_1\right)\left(r + r_p\right)\left(r - r_0\right)}\dot{t}\dot{r} = 0

\ddot{r} + \dfrac{\left(r - r_0\right)\left(r^2\,r_0 + r^2\,r_1 + r^2\,r_p + 2r\,r_1\,r_p - r_0\,r_1\,r_p\right)}{2r\left(r + r_1\right)^2\left(r + r_p\right)^2}\dot{t}^2 - \dfrac{r_0}{2r\left(r - r_0\right)}\dot{r}^2 - \left(r - r_0\right)\dot{\theta}^2 - \left(r - r_0\right)\sin^2\theta\,\dot{\phi}^2 = 0
